opportunity: kuna's `inferfuncentry` escape (GH-6930) suspends ActionConstantPtr's `bit_transitions < 3` guard for any constant that resolves to an exact function entry, whatever the operand means. In a position-independent executable `.init` sits at a low round offset, so a round buffer size lands on one: coreutils tail -O0 computes MIN (n_remaining, BUFSIZ), BUFSIZ is 0x2000 and 0x2000 is that image's _DT_INIT, so the bound printed as `if (_DT_INIT < v9)`, the other arm of the select as `v1 = _DT_INIT`, and the uintmax_t byte counter they bounded became `void *` -- in dump_remainder, and through protoorder in tail_forever's `uintmax_t bytes_to_read`.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-inferfuncentry-intbound.xml (5 assertions, four passes: the bounded value, its bound, the GH-6930 callback argument, a function-pointer COPY control, and the option-off control) + 5 unit tests in p5_types/kuna_inferfuncentry/tests.rs
change_kind: strict bug fix, no option (it narrows the existing `inferfuncentry` rule; `inferfuncentry off` still means upstream)

misattribution_checked.claim: the two rows that moved the wrong way between the round-B and round-C campaign measurements were attributed to `ptrfromuse void`
misattribution_checked.ablation: 444-slice typesweep `--option ptrfromuse off` on main 2e28ece4a: PERFECT 1349 -> 1145 (-204), moved ONTO perfect 0, improved 0, worsened 85. ptrfromuse-void has no measurable false positive on that corpus.
misattribution_checked.tail_forever: 0.75 in BOTH arms of that ablation; `bytes_to_read` is `void *` with ptrfromuse off and stays `void *` with protoorder / structsynth / charbyte / boolbyte / foldcallretphi / codescalar / formatstring / libctypes off. Only `inferfuncentry off` changes it. The round-B binary already printed `void *` for dump_remainder; what round C added was protoorder carrying that wrong callee type to the caller.
misattribution_checked.buf_has_encoding_errors: 0.2 in BOTH arms. `buf` is `unsigned long *`, not `void *`: skip_easy_bytes reads a uword at a time, so that pointee is what the callee's body says and protoorder carries it. A pointee-granularity question, out of this fix's scope.

rule.reads_as_integer: INT_LESS / INT_LESSEQUAL / INT_SLESS / INT_SLESSEQUAL / INT_MULT / INT_DIV / INT_SDIV / INT_REM / INT_SREM / INT_LEFT / INT_RIGHT / INT_SRIGHT
rule.orders_its_constant: the four comparisons; a bound also pins the value one below its literal, because the strict/non-strict rewrite moves it (tail's MIN arrives as INT_LESS(0x2000, n), head's as INT_LESS(0x2001, n))
rule.entry_escape_applies: the escape is available when this reader is not one of those AND the same numeric value is not read as one anywhere else in the function
rule.why_the_reader_alone_is_not_enough: the assignment arm of a MIN is a plain COPY and so is every entry of a function-pointer table. coreutils od -O2 decode_one_format selects between sub_3f20, sub_3ff0, sub_40a0 and sub_4150, and 0x3ff0 is the one of the four with fewer than three bit transitions: refusing the escape on COPY alone left `v4 = (void *)0x3ff0;` among three named siblings (measured on an earlier revision of this branch).
rule.cost: the set of numerically-read values is built once per ActionConstantPtr pass from the constant snapshot apply() already takes: one lone_descend per constant

benchmark.slice_set: projects coreutils grep gzip diffutils bzip2 findutils tar shadow, O0/O2/O2-noinline: 444 slices, 10,748 functions

rebase_remeasure.why: argclobber changes call argument lists, so both arms were re-measured on the rebased tree
rebase_remeasure.note: identical to the 2e28ece4a measurement: argclobber moves no type_match row on this slice set
rebase_remeasure.hunk_reclassification: coreutils tail/head/od/seq at O0, base arm vs fix arm: od unchanged, the other three are the same cast-change / declaration / renumbering classes as the original bundle, no statement moved or deleted

corpus_diff.surface: whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` C, main vs the fix, 16 builds (coreutils head/od/seq/tail/ls, grep, gzip, tar at O0 and O2), 6,882 functions
corpus_diff.OTHER: all 55 are the one class: a byte counter that was wrongly a pointer becomes an integer, so `&v[-n]` becomes `v -= n`, `(void *)0xffffffffffffffff` becomes `-1`, `NULL` becomes `0`, `(void *)0xa` becomes `10`, and `_DT_INIT` becomes `0x2000`. The classifier's skeleton normalizer cannot equate a symbol with a literal, which is why they land in its catch-all bucket.
corpus_diff.STATEMENT: all 4 are one declaration block moving because a `void *` became `unsigned long` and the block re-sorts; nothing is deleted (`char v10; bool v11; void *v12;` -> `char v8; bool v9;` + `unsigned long v39;`). This is the classifier's documented `bool` blind spot, recorded in docs/features/ptrfromuse/record.json.

speed.method: interleaved whole-binary `decompile-all --json`, min-of-15 and median-of-15, alternating arm order; deltas over +5% re-run at a quieter moment with min-of-21
speed.verdict: within budget. gzip-O2 brackets zero (+7.13% then -7.09%), so the effect is under this box's noise floor; the worst credible number is ls-O2 at +1.79%.

notes: The lane was briefed to tighten `ptrfromuse`'s refusal on a value used as an integer. The premise did not survive measurement (see misattribution_checked), and the defect the brief pointed at is real but belongs to `inferfuncentry`. The fix keeps the brief's rule -- a value the function uses as a number is not committed to a pointer -- at the place that was actually committing it.
